title: PHRASAL VERBS
notes:
✓ Phrasal verb → a verb combined with one or more particles (usually an adverb or preposition) to create a new meaning.

✓ Structure → verb + particle
✓ give + up → give up
✓ look + after → look after
✓ turn + on → turn on

✓ The meaning of a phrasal verb is often different from the meaning of the main verb alone.

✓ look → use your eyes
✓ look after → take care of

title: COMMON PHRASAL VERBS: DAILY LIFE
notes:
✓ wake up → stop sleeping
Example → I wake up at 6 a.m.

✓ get up → leave your bed
Example → She gets up early.

✓ sit down → take a seat
Example → Please sit down.

✓ stand up → rise to your feet
Example → Everyone stood up.

✓ go out → leave home / go somewhere for entertainment
Example → We went out last night.

✓ come back → return
Example → He came back late.

title: PHRASAL VERBS: MOVEMENT
notes:
✓ come in → enter
✓ go in → enter
✓ get in → enter a car/taxi or arrive
✓ get out → leave a vehicle/place
✓ come back → return
✓ go back → return to a place/state
✓ move on → continue or progress
✓ turn back → return in the direction you came from

✓ Come in and sit down.
✓ We had to turn back because of the rain.
✓ After finishing the task, we moved on.

title: PHRASAL VERBS: COMMUNICATION
notes:
✓ call back → return a phone call
✓ call off → cancel
✓ speak up → speak more loudly
✓ bring up → introduce a topic
✓ point out → draw attention to something
✓ find out → discover information
✓ ask around → ask several people for information
✓ get back to → contact someone again later

✓ I'll call you back later.
✓ She pointed out my mistake.
✓ We need to find out what happened.

title: PHRASAL VERBS: WORK & STUDY
notes:
✓ hand in → submit
✓ hand out → distribute
✓ look up → search for information
✓ go over → review/check carefully
✓ work out → solve/understand
✓ carry out → perform/conduct
✓ take on → accept responsibility/work
✓ catch up → reach the same level as someone/something
✓ keep up → maintain the same speed or level

✓ Hand in your assignment tomorrow.
✓ I looked up the word in a dictionary.
✓ The researchers carried out an experiment.

title: PHRASAL VERBS: PROBLEMS & SOLUTIONS
notes:
✓ deal with → handle/manage
✓ sort out → solve or organize a problem
✓ work out → find a solution
✓ figure out → understand/solve
✓ get over → recover from a problem or disappointment
✓ break down → stop working / fail
✓ run out of → have no more left
✓ put off → postpone
✓ give up → stop trying

✓ We need to sort out this problem.
✓ I can't figure out the answer.
✓ We've run out of water.
✓ Don't give up.

title: PHRASAL VERBS: RELATIONSHIPS & PEOPLE
notes:
✓ get along with → have a good relationship
✓ fall out with → have an argument/disagreement
✓ look after → take care of
✓ look up to → admire/respect
✓ look down on → consider someone inferior
✓ get together → meet socially
✓ break up → end a romantic relationship
✓ make up → become friendly again after an argument

✓ I get along well with my classmates.
✓ She looks up to her teacher.
✓ They made up after the argument.

title: SEPARABLE PHRASAL VERBS
notes:
✓ In separable phrasal verbs, the object can come between the verb and particle.

✓ turn off the light
✓ turn the light off

✓ pick up the phone
✓ pick the phone up

✓ With a noun object, both positions may be possible for many separable verbs.

⚠️ With a pronoun, the object normally MUST come between the verb and particle.

❌ Turn off it.
✓ Turn it off.

❌ Pick up it.
✓ Pick it up.

title: INSEPARABLE PHRASAL VERBS
notes:
✓ In inseparable phrasal verbs, the verb and particle/preposition stay together.

✓ look after someone
✓ look into something
✓ get over something
✓ run into someone
✓ deal with something

❌ Look your brother after.
✓ Look after your brother.

❌ Deal the problem with.
✓ Deal with the problem.

title: THREE-WORD PHRASAL VERBS
notes:
✓ Some phrasal verbs contain three words: verb + particle + preposition.

✓ look forward to → anticipate
✓ get along with → have a good relationship
✓ look up to → admire
✓ look down on → consider inferior
✓ put up with → tolerate
✓ run out of → have no more
✓ get rid of → remove/dispose of
✓ come up with → think of/produce an idea

✓ I look forward to meeting you.
✓ She came up with a good idea.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'GET'
notes:
✓ get up → rise from bed
✓ get in → enter/arrive
✓ get out → leave
✓ get back → return
✓ get over → recover
✓ get along with → have a good relationship
✓ get rid of → remove
✓ get through → successfully finish/survive
✓ get by → manage with difficulty
✓ get away → escape/leave

✓ 'Get' forms many high-frequency phrasal verbs, so learn each as a complete expression.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'TAKE'
notes:
✓ take off → remove / plane leaves the ground
✓ take on → accept responsibility or work
✓ take up → begin a hobby/activity
✓ take over → take control
✓ take back → return something / withdraw a statement
✓ take after → resemble a family member
✓ take out → remove / go somewhere with someone

✓ The plane took off on time.
✓ She took up swimming last year.
✓ He takes after his father.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'LOOK'
notes:
✓ look at → examine/watch
✓ look for → search for
✓ look after → take care of
✓ look up → search for information
✓ look into → investigate
✓ look out → be careful
✓ look forward to → anticipate
✓ look up to → admire
✓ look down on → regard as inferior

✓ I'm looking for my keys.
✓ The police are looking into the case.
✓ I look forward to hearing from you.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'PUT'
notes:
✓ put on → wear
✓ put off → postpone
✓ put away → return something to its proper place
✓ put out → extinguish
✓ put up → display / provide accommodation
✓ put up with → tolerate
✓ put down → place on a surface / criticize
✓ put forward → suggest or present an idea

✓ Put on your jacket.
✓ They put off the meeting.
✓ I can't put up with the noise.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'BREAK'
notes:
✓ break down → stop functioning / collapse
✓ break up → end a relationship / separate
✓ break out → start suddenly, especially something unpleasant
✓ break into → enter by force
✓ break through → succeed in overcoming a barrier
✓ break away → escape/separate

✓ My car broke down.
✓ A fire broke out last night.
✓ Someone broke into the house.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'TURN'
notes:
✓ turn on → switch on
✓ turn off → switch off
✓ turn up → increase volume / arrive unexpectedly
✓ turn down → decrease volume / reject
✓ turn into → become/change into
✓ turn back → return
✓ turn out → result / prove to be

✓ Turn off the light.
✓ Please turn down the music.
✓ The event turned out well.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH 'COME' & 'GO'
notes:
✓ come across → find or meet unexpectedly
✓ come up with → think of an idea
✓ come back → return
✓ come in → enter
✓ come out → become available / leave a place

✓ go on → continue
✓ go over → review
✓ go through → experience/examine
✓ go ahead → proceed
✓ go back → return

✓ I came across an interesting article.
✓ Please go ahead with the plan.

title: PHRASAL VERBS WITH MULTIPLE MEANINGS
notes:
✓ One phrasal verb can have different meanings depending on context.

✓ take off → remove clothes
Example → Take off your shoes.

✓ take off → a plane leaves the ground
Example → The plane took off.

✓ work out → exercise
Example → I work out every morning.

✓ work out → solve/be successful
Example → Everything worked out well.

✓ Always understand the context before choosing the meaning.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ Turn off it.
✓ Turn it off.

❌ Look my brother after.
✓ Look after my brother.

❌ I am looking my keys for.
✓ I am looking for my keys.

❌ She gave smoking up.
✓ She gave up smoking.

❌ We ran water out of.
✓ We ran out of water.

❌ I look forward to meet you.
✓ I look forward to meeting you.

✓ Learn the complete structure of each phrasal verb, including whether it is separable and what preposition follows it.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Phrasal verb → verb + particle/preposition with a special meaning.

◆ 2. Learn phrasal verbs as complete expressions, not as individual words.

◆ 3. Check whether the phrasal verb is separable or inseparable.

◆ 4. With separable verbs + pronoun → pronoun goes between the verb and particle.
✓ Turn it off.

◆ 5. Three-word phrasal verbs normally stay together.
✓ She gets along with her classmates.

◆ 6. Watch for context because one phrasal verb may have several meanings.

◆ 7. Common exam phrasal verbs → give up, look after, look for, find out, put off, call off, carry out, run out of, get along with, take over, turn down, work out, break down, come up with, deal with.

✓ Golden rule → Don't translate a phrasal verb word-by-word; learn its complete meaning and grammatical pattern.
